I'm going into the forum and seeing that a common request is "how do i stop my shower curtain rail squeek?". Well to be fair that's an extremely easy one.

When installing a new rod, or if the current rail isn`t aligned with a door frame for instance (and is therefore loose and moving) - that could very quickly be an underlying culprit to a squeaking sound from that area. In order to correct such, first remove or adjust to make that alignment straight with your walls/ceilling.

Once aligned with the door opening you will have more rigidy. This is key for stopping those squeak issues from the curtain pole, but if your current curtain track/ring system already seems well-aligned and is in the same area, it can help as the rod and rings can move against another.

If you're noticing movement of either the ring/rails themselves (like one part is loose) - that could lead to a caked in soap build - so make certain the area you're looking at isn not overly wet and soiled (and you might have to scrub the ring to get rid that build).

However - most people just have their rings
